New CIP Projects

New Projects: (in recommended priority order) • Campus Accessibility – This project, would provide dedicated resources to improve campus access to persons with disabilities.
Projects include restroom improvements, exterior pedestrian improvements, and discrete building improvements such as elevator modernizations.
URI has 80 elevators.
Of these, 19 are more than 30 years old and only 18 are newer than 10 years.
Many of our buildings are served by single units.
The combination of single units and aged equipment often results in downtime and limits access.
This level of support would allow for the modernization of 2-3 units per year or the replacement of one.
Funding source is RICAP - $16.5MM (FY26/27 @ $3MM FY28-30 @ $3.5MM each year) • Building Envelope Improvements – Many of the campus buildings have envelopes, including roofing systems, that are far past their serviceable life.
With water intrusion active in many locations, protecting these facilities from the damage that this causes and ensuring that environmental conditions remain safe for occupancy, this project addresses critical concerns now present on campus.

Funding source is RICAP - $53MM over 4 years • Carothers HVAC Replacement – The initial core structure of the Library was constructed in 1965 and renovated in two supplemental phases in the early ‘90s.
The current structure is 252,792 gross square feet on five floors with 175 assignable spaces.
Many air handling units are original to the building, have well exceeded their expected 30-year lifetime, and are in relatively poor condition which can adversely affect air quality.
Funding source is RICAP - $64.3MM starting in FY26 • Campus Access Control – Current evaluation of a university-wide Access Control systems is underway.
In order to provide a safer campus environment, there will be a need to update the software and hardware systems to allow for a secure campus and quick responses to emergencies such as lockdown for an active shooter event.
Total Project Cost and Schedule TBD.
Funding source is RICAP - $1.5MM (just FY26) for initial conversion to a uniform system for the campus.
Future support will be needed to tie in all buildings to this centralized system over time.

Future support level TBD • New Graduate Housing – If the Public Private Partnership does not proceed to deliver critical graduate housing, this project would replace Graduate Village and deliver 200-beds to meet the immediate need.
Based on recent market conditions, this project would require $154.1MM.
Funding source is RIHEBC in FY26

New Projects: (in recommended priority order) • Automotive & Administrative Services – To complete the creation of the new housing district on the western edge of campus and provide proper working space for Automotive and Mail & Printing Services, this project builds an addition to the Central Warehouse for Mail/Printing and provides a new Automotive repair building that replaces the current Automotive building that was once an animal barn.
Funding source is RIHEBC - $14.4MM in FY27 • Public Safety Building – The current Public Safety operations are located in three buildings, spread across the Kingston Campus, two of which are converted residential houses.
This project would combine all of these into one efficient building across from the Ryan Center.
The University Policy Department exercises full municipal-level police powers.
Police and other Public Safety personnel are the University’s first responders to situations that occur on University property while serving to promote safe practices across the community.

Funding source is RICAP - $48.3MM over 4 years starting in FY27 • NBC Shoreline Stabilization – The Bay Campus has seen significant shoreline erosion over the past 6 months as storms have intensified and hit the area directly adjacent to Pier Road, our only accessway to the new Pier.
Having already contracted with the Army Corp of Engineers, URI is looking at possible ways to secure this area so that this critical roadway is not undermined and taken out of service.
We expect that this current study will result in a $6.4MM Total Project Cost that is 35% funded with RI state funding (RICAP) ($2.24MM) and 65% federal sources ($4.16MM) • Water Tower – Built in 1971, the current water tower requires refurbishment, which will be supported by one of the Utility RIHEBC bonds.
In addition, additional water capacity is needed to support the expanding campus footprint and fire compliance needs.
Recommend building new tower after refurbishing existing tower.
Funding source is RICAP - $10.7MM over 3 years starting in FY29

It would provide modern grandstands including press box, 5,240 seats (6,596 total capacity with west stands), restrooms, concessions, field level training and taping room, equipment storage and full ADA compliance. • $42,800,000 - RICAP • Status: Design Phase Kicked off in March 2024 • Start 2023 • Complete 2027 Kingston Campus - Locus Map Meade East Grandstand Replacement Ongoing Approved Project

Project Statistics: • This maintains the track in the same general footprint reducing the costs and the need to displace any other fields or amenities within the existing athletic complex. This concept keeps the track in a north/south orientation but proposes to switch the common finish line to the northeast corner, which would allow athletes to finish most events with the prevailing winds at their backs. In the event winds change during a meet, the opposite finish line could be utilized based on the proposed layout. This concept proposes to remove several existing older buildings and a maintenance storage area close to the complex entrance off the northeast corner of the track. The removal of these buildings will ultimately create space for an ADA parking lot and a cleaner and more visually appealing entrance to the site. • $ 12,200,000 - RICAP • Status: Design Phase Kicked off in March 2024 • Start 2023 • Complete 2026 Kingston Campus - Locus Map Track & Field Replacement Ongoing Approved Project

Project Statistics: • In 2020 the University completed an advanced planning study for the replacement of the Tootell pools with a new natatorium building. Review of the Governor’s FY2025 Recommended Budget Enclosure 2.a.
Vice Chair Sabitoni introduced Abby Benson, Interim Vice President for Administration and Finance who provided a presentation on the Governor’s FY2025 Recommended Budget.
This presentation can be found in Enclosure 2.a.
Her presentation included discussions of the University’s FY2025 Appropriation Request, with respect to the FY2024 request and enacted amounts; details regarding the University’s current service level; strategic initiatives; RICAP; and the pending General Obligation Bond (Biomedical Life Sciences Building). b.
Tuition and Fee Rates Review Enclosure 2.b.
Interim Vice President Benson provided a presentation on tuition and fees for FY 2025.
The presentation can be found in Enclosure 2.b.
She noted that the Board had approved permanently moving the approval of tuition and fees from the September meeting to the February meeting.

Interim Vice President Benson’s presentation covered the total cost of attendance (TCOA) (noting the assumptions used in this calculation) by discussing 1) Housing and Dining rates, noting a 3.6% increase in these areas collectively, 2) mandatory fees, noting a 0.9% fee increase overall, and 3) tuition.
Interim VP Benson introduced Dean Libutti, Associate Vice President for Enrollment Management and Student Success, who discussed enrollment planning for FY2025, noting zero changes to the FY2025 First-Year target (with a small shift between in-state and out-of-state students) and a forty-five-student decrease in transfers.
He also presented assumptions regarding enrollments across the University.
Interim Vice President Benson provided a recommendation to the Committee for a 3.5% increase in tuition across the board, noting that this amount provides maximum revenue while managing potential enrollment declines.
She discussed the assumptions used for building this model.
Dean Libutti noted that the assumptions used in this model are based on macroeconomic analyses, internal data, and anecdotal information from URI students and parents.

Interim Vice President Benson introduced John Poehlmann, Assistant Vice President for Financial Strategy and Planning, who discussed URI’s TCOA compared to URI’s regional peers.
In addition, he provided detail on modeling scenarios for undergraduate and graduate populations that provided for the recommended tuition increase.
In addition, John Poehlmann discussed strategies for expanding graduate enrollments.
